                    ### Question
                    A 32-year-old woman comes to her doctor’s office with abdominal distention, diffuse abdominal pain, and a history of 10–12 bowel movements a day for the last week. She was diagnosed with Crohn’s disease 3 years ago. Today, vitals are normal. Her abdomen is mildly distended and diffusely tender to palpation. A CT scan shows evidence of a fistula and strictures located in the last 30 cm of her ileum. A resection of the affected portion of the bowel is scheduled. What changes in bile metabolism are expected in this patient post-procedure?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Absorption of vitamin K will not be impaired
opb. Synthesis of cholesterol in the liver will decrease
opc. The balance of the components in bile will be altered
opd. Enteric bacteria will remain the same in the small intestine
ope. Absorption of  7⍺-dehydroxylated bile will decrease

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Resection of the ileum leads to decreased absorption of bile acids due to the loss of the terminal ileum, which is crucial for bile acid reabsorption. This results in altered bile metabolism, specifically an imbalance in bile components, as the recycling of bile acids is impaired. Therefore, option (opc) is correct: the balance of the components in bile will be altered. Option (opa) is incorrect because absorption of vitamin K will be impaired due to the loss of ileal function, which is essential for the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins. Option (opb) is not directly relevant to bile metabolism changes post-resection. Option (opd) is incorrect as bacterial overgrowth is likely to occur post-resection, affecting bile acid metabolism. Lastly, option (ope) is correct; absorption of 7α-dehydroxylated bile acids will decrease due to reduced ileal absorption capacity. Thus, the most relevant and correct options are (opc) and (ope).
